item.title: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has blamed his political opponents for hunger and poverty in Nigeria, insisting that his administration is working to address the challenges. Tinubu spoke on Saturday at the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign flag-off rally at Ranchers Bees Stadium, also known as Kaduna Township Stadium, in Kaduna State, ahead of the 2027 general elections. “I have an argument. I hear my opponent talking about hunger, poverty. Who created it? They did! They created the hunger, they created the poverty. We are trying to eradicate it,” the president said. He also defended his administration’s record on salary payments and commended state governors for their performance, saying they were making progress in their respective states. “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing,” Tinubu said. The president thanked Kaduna residents for supporting him in the previous presidential election, saying their votes contributed to his emergence as president. “You gave me joy to remember the victory you gave me to become president. I come again to thank you,” he said. Tinubu appealed to Nigerians to give him another term, saying he wanted to sustain his promises of prosperity, continuity, progress and development. item.title: EPL: Arsenal see off Everton, go joint-top after Man City defeat
item.description: Manchester City’s flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery’s men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side. Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game. “We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box,” said Maresca. The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window. But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong. The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes. Another of Villa’s new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves. Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise. Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson’s low shot on the hour mark. “A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park,” said Emery. “We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic.” – Arsenal’s set-piece prowess – Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton. Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done. Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta’s men midway through the second period. Fulham further eased the pressure on manager Alvaro Arbeloa with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb’s individual effort. A second consecutive victory propels the Cottagers out of the relegation zone and up to 12th. Tottenham are also seeking to escape the bottom three when they travel to Chelsea in the evening kick-off, aiming to improve on a terrible record at Stamford Bridge. On Sunday the focus turns on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth. A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick’s future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season. item.title: Como follow Man Utd thumping with victory in Serie A
item.description: Como backed up their brilliant Champions League victory over Manchester United as Anastasios Douvikas scored twice in a 2-0 Serie A win against Sassuolo on Saturday. Cesc Fabregas’s side climbed to fourth in the table, just two points adrift of early leaders Inter Milan who host Fiorentina on Sunday. Como were frustrated for long periods by a stubborn Sassuolo team, but clinched an ultimately comfortable win courtesy of Douvikas’s two goals in the space of 11 second-half minutes. The Greece striker has now scored five goals in his last four games, and eight in all competitions in total this season. Como, who qualified for Europe for the first time in their history last term, thrashed Man United 4-1 in the Champions League in midweek. Later Saturday, Roma bid to go top of the table when they visit Napoli, before second-placed Lazio also eye the summit in their home game against Parma. From collapsing shops overtaken by weeds to deplorable internal roads, heaps of refuse, poor sanitation and the absence of electricity, water and banking facilities, the once-bustling market has become a symbol of dashed hopes for traders who say their compliance with the government’s relocation order has left them economically stranded. They are now appealing to Governor Alex Otti to urgently intervene before the market, which was conceived as the commercial hub of Umuahia, collapses completely. During a visit to the market by Vanguard, traders recounted painful experiences, describing a deteriorating commercial environment in which some struggle to cover their daily expenses. ‘This market does not look six months old’ A provisions dealer, Mr Ugochukwu Okeke, popularly known as Onwa, identified poor internal roads, lack of electricity, declining patronage and the absence of the promised alternative access road via Umueze as major challenges confronting traders. He said the failure to construct the proposed Ubani–Agbo–Umueze Road had continued to expose road users to the dangers of the busy Umuahia–Uzuakoli Road. ” In 2013 when we were asked to relocate to this place, Government promised to build a shorter route to the market passing through Umueze and Agbo to make it easily accessible from the city but up till today we have not seen it. The other day, a trader was returning to the City after the day’s sales and boarded a tricycle. On their way through the busy Uzuakoli road, a trailer had a break failure and rammed into the Keke. The head of the woman was cut off immediately as a result of the impact. That woman wouldn’t have lost her life if the road Ubani-Agbo -Umueze Road were fixed as promised earlier by Government 13 years ago. ” Another challenge we face here is poor sales due to continued decline in the number of people coming to shop here. This is because of the existence of markets around Isigate. Many traders have continued to pull out of the market back to town and government is doing nothing but just watching helplessly. This is affecting the few of us that are here. ” This is 13 years we were forced to come here but this market does not look as if it has lasted for six months because it is going down everyday.” Beyond the physical deterioration, Okeke said the absence of banks in and around the market had created security risks for traders who handle cash from daily sales. He recalled an incident in which a neighbouring trader allegedly lost a carton containing money after hiding it among refuse to prevent thieves from stealing the proceeds of his business. ” My neighbour sometime ago lost his carton of money here. He was putting the proceeds of the day’s sales inside the cartoon and kept it in the midst of refuse to avoid being stolen because there is no Bank in the market. Afterwards he collected a carton of refuse thinking it was the one containing money. On getting home he discovered he had forgotten his money outside and tili today he has not found it back.” The trader also faulted the collection of an annual consolidated levy of ₦36,000 per shop, saying the financial burden had become difficult to bear amid poor sales.He appealed to the government to make the levy payable per trader rather than per shop, as he said was currently the practice. ” Last year they came and said we will be paying N36,000 per annum promising to use the revenue to solve our problems. We paid. The worst thing is that they are collecting this revenue based on the number of shops a trader has in the market. Although we pay, we don’t yet see anything they are doing with it. ” I’m not sure the Governor is aware of this. That’s why I’m appealing to him to look into what is happening at Ubani Ultra-modern Market. We are suffering here. We are just merely surviving by God’s grace. There is no future for this market as long as the same Government continues to allow some traders return to Isigate. We heard that revenue collectors collect revenues from the traders there twice a day. That’s why they are not serious about forcing them out of that place. We are the ones suffering it here”. ‘Our business capital is depreciating’ A patent medicine dealer, Mr Michael Ubani, said the market’s fortunes would continue to decline unless the government enforced its relocation policy and addressed the infrastructure deficit. He said traders who obeyed the relocation directive had been left to bear the consequences while competing markets continued to operate within the city centre. ” We are hopelessly struggling to survive here. This is a stranded place for us because of its distance from the City metropolis. Government is not looking our way. Every effort to get Government’s attention to this market has been fruitless. You can see that traders are pulling from the market on daily basis due to lack of patronage. ” Amenities here are zero – no internal roads, no electricity. The Umueze – Agbo -Ubani road which would have provided a shorter route to the market is a total mess. item.title: Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has charged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) deployed to the state to avoid partisan politics in their host communities. Aiyedatiwa gave the charge at the closing ceremony and terminal parade of the 2026 Batch C Stream I orientation course held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the State Coordinator of the scheme, Mrs Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, the governor urged the corps members to be conscious of their responsibilities. “Remain mindful of the responsibilities that come with your position as corps members. Your actions will reflect not only on you but also on your families, your institutions and the NYSC,” he said. He appealed to employers and heads of establishments to receive corps members posted to them with cooperation and understanding. “Provide them with a conducive working environment, appropriate guidance and opportunities to contribute their knowledge and skills. Your mentorship can help them grow professionally and gain valuable experience that will serve them well beyond their service year,” Aiyedatiwa said. He also called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and community leaders to support corps members in their areas to aid their integration and effective execution of Community Development Service projects. “Your cooperation is essential to their successful integration into host communities and to the effective implementation of Community Development Service projects. By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. Be willing to learn from your host communities, respect their customs and cultural values and conduct yourselves in ways that will earn their trust and confidence. “Your service year should be about more than fulfilling an obligation. It should be an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Aiyedatiwa assured that his administration will continue to collaborate with security agencies and other stakeholders to ensure a safe environment for corps members throughout the service year. He cautioned them against compromising their personal security, advising them to remain vigilant, avoid late-night movements and unsafe gatherings, and shun unsolicited rides from strangers. “Be cautious when visiting unfamiliar or isolated places and promptly report suspicious activities or security concerns to the appropriate authorities. “Shun drug abuse, cybercrime, fraud and other unlawful activities that could jeopardise your future and bring disrepute to the scheme,” the governor added.

item.title: Tinubu, Shettima flag off APC 2027 campaign in Kaduna
item.description: President Bola Tinubu arrived in Kaduna State on Saturday ahead of the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress’ 2027 presidential campaign, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana, also arriving for the event. APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, the Director-General of the presidential campaign, Abdul’aziz Yari, and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani were at the airport to welcome the President. Shettima’s arrival was announced in a statement by his spokesman, Stanley Nkwocha. Mr Nkwocha said APC governors, party leaders, elected officials, political stakeholders and supporters were gathering at the Kaduna Township Stadium for the commencement of the party’s nationwide presidential campaign. He described the event as a significant moment for Kaduna, noting that the city would serve as the launching point for the APC’s campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election. According to the statement, the campaign would provide the ruling party with an opportunity to present its “Renewed Hope 2.0” agenda and highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration. “The stage is set. Kaduna is ready. The 2027 campaign begins!” the statement read in part. It added, “Asiwaju is here. Northwest for the takeaway!” Ahead of the President’s arrival, security operatives on Saturday barricaded strategic locations across Kaduna metropolis as authorities stepped up security preparations for the campaign event. Personnel from the Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Nigeria Immigration Service and the Kaduna State Vigilance Service were deployed to different parts of the city. The security personnel were stationed at major roundabouts and along roads leading to the venue of the campaign flag-off. Muhammadu Buhari Way, formerly known as WAFF Road, was blocked by security operatives ahead of the expected movement of the President and his entourage through the route. The Ahmadu Bello Stadium roundabout was also manned by heavily armed soldiers, police officers and plain-clothes security personnel. The security restrictions affected traffic in several parts of Kaduna, triggering a gridlock that extended from Junction Road to Ahmadu Bello Way. item.title: French Montana, Jorja Smith to perform at Ballon d’Or 2026
item.description: Ballon d’Or organisers revealed on Saturday that star US rapper French Montana and English singer Jorja Smith would perform at this year’s ceremony, part of efforts to draw more viewers to the awards event. Last year saw Canadian singer Charlotte Cardin do her best to lift the somewhat stiff atmosphere at the prize giving in Paris as she performed her hit “Feel Good” in front of a motionless crowd of suited footballers and VIPs at a theatre. The most prestigious individual award in football will be handed out in London next Monday, with Kylian Mbappe, Spanish pair Lamine Yamal and Ferran Torres, PSG duo Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Harry Kane all seen as frontrunners. It is the first time the Ballon d’Or ceremony, now in its 70th edition, will be hosted in Britain. French Montana has over 30 million monthly listeners on Spotify, mixing Moroccan influences, trap, afrobeat and New York hip hop culture. He has collaborated on hits with Drake, Cardi B and Swae Lee, with whom he made the 2017 track “Unforgettable”, which has racked up 1.9 billion views on YouTube. English singer-songwriter Jorja Smith mixes RnB, soul and jazz influences, drawing on her Jamaican heritage and her classical music training. Her career took off 10 years ago with “Blue Lights”, followed by other tracks ranging from intimate to more danceable. In addition to their “exclusive performances” during the evening, “other surprises are planned”, the Groupe L’Equipe, which organises the ceremony, said in a statement sent to AFP. The group owns the magazine France Football, which has been awarding the Ballon d’Or since 1956. It is based on voting by a jury of journalists from the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings. In 2025, the top male player prize was awarded to France’s Ousmane Dembele and the women’s to Spain’s Aitana Bonmati. The ceremony will be broadcast on sports streaming website DAZN, and the L’Equipe TV channel in France. It will be hosted by former France and Arsenal striker Thierry Henry, and sports journalist Kate Scott. In 2022, tenor Andrea Bocelli was chosen to open the ceremony. After last year’s event, Quebec-born Cardin revealed that she had felt uneasy, explaining that she had been through a “moment of great solitude” when she performed alone with limited lighting and stage effects. fan-adp/gil The post French Montana, Jorja Smith to perform at Ballon d’Or 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start
item.description: Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson’s double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery’s new-look side. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay. Erling Haaland breifly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye’s cross. Four years on from Emery’s arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into the Champions League, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated. Six of the side that started Villa’s victory in last season’s Europa League left during the transfer window. But the recruitment of the likes of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign. Until now City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club’s Premier League future to keep winning on the field. The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation. There was little sign of that distraction affecting Enzo Maresca’s men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors. A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma. City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki. Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post. City’s pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye’s cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season. Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive into the crossbar moments later. Instead, it was Villa to got the decisive third goal. Mbaye was played in behind the City defence and from his cross, Jackson’s low effort should have been saved by Donnarumma. The visitors pressed in vain for another equaliser to allow Arsenal the chance to move level on points at the top of the table when they host Everton later on Saturday. A sixth win in seven games in all competitions for Villa lifts them up to sixth. The post Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start appeared first on Vanguard News .

If Asiwaju was not a good leader, I would not tell you otherwise. I will still come to Kaduna to speak with you. Your governor is a good man, and he has done well for this state. Let us return him to power too,” he said. item.title: Troops neutralise 15 terrorists in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), has recorded another operational success with the neutralisation of 15 terrorists in a precision air strike north-west of Pulka in Gwoza LGA of Borno State. According to the Media Information Officer Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni, in a press statement on Saturday, said, “The operation was conducted at about 11:50 p.m. on 23 October 2026, following credible intelligence and confirmed sightings of terrorist movements in the general area of Pulka. “The precision strike was subsequently followed by ground operations to exploit the area and consolidate the operational gains. “The successful engagement highlights the effectiveness of intelligence-driven targeting and coordinated military action in disrupting terrorist movements and degrading their operational capabilities. “It also reflects the unwavering commitment of Operation HADIN KAI to denying terrorist groups freedom of action and preventing them from threatening communities within the theatre. “The operation forms part of the sustained offensive posture of troops, supported by effective intelligence gathering and coordinated employment of available military capabilities. The continued partnership between the military and the civilian population remains essential to consolidating operational gains and achieving lasting peace and security across the Northeast.” Goni explained. item.title: Thousands March In France Against Far-Right Party Congress
item.description: Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the French city of Orléans Saturday against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw. The protest — held on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living after ones a week ago that devolved into street violence — criticised both Le Pen and centrist President Emmanuel Macron. France’s President Emmanuel Macron meets with elected officials at the town hall following a shooting in Trappes, near Paris, on October 23, 2026. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled, while carrying placards that read “The Youth say ‘screw you’ to the National Rally” and “Hotter than fascists”. The two-day RN congress in Orleans was the first big party campaign rally by Le Pen, whom surveys put as the leading candidate to succeed Macron in presidential elections in six months. It is a major political centre in the North-West, but it is not naturally secure territory for the President. Tinubu lost Kaduna to Atiku Abubakar in 2023. The state also embodies several issues that could determine northern voting behaviour: insecurity, rural poverty, food prices, religious sensitivity and the relationship between elite political agreements and popular sentiment. By beginning there, the APC is signalling that it will not concede the region to Atiku merely because he is a northern Muslim. It is relying on Vice-President Kashim Shettima, governors, ministers, traditional relationships and a greatly expanded party structure to offset Atiku’s regional appeal. That structure matters. The APC now enjoys an extraordinary advantage in the number of governors, lawmakers and local political networks under its control. Governors influence campaign financing, mobilisation and the organisation required to convert public sympathy into votes. The party’s challenge is that political machinery can mobilise supporters, but it cannot permanently insulate an incumbent from lived economic experience. The contest between structure and hardship The APC’s campaign argument will be that the most painful period of reform has passed. Inflation has moderated, foreign reserves have improved, economic growth has strengthened, and the Central Bank has begun adjusting interest rates. The administration will argue that removing the petrol subsidy and reforming the foreign-exchange market prevented a deeper fiscal crisis. The opposition’s reply is more immediate: food, transport, energy and business costs remain painfully high. That explains the political significance of the National Economic Council’s newly approved 90-day action plan. It prioritises food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, removal of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. It also proposes a national dashboard to track projects and the use of savings from subsidy removal. On paper, these are reasonable interventions. The problem is timing. The presidential election is 86 days away, while the relief plan is designed to run for 90 days. Atiku’s campaign has therefore called it “election bait,” arguing that Nigerians are being asked to vote before the promised relief can be fully assessed. That is a partisan allegation, not proof that the programme is improper. But the calendar gives the criticism political force. The government can answer it only through early, measurable delivery. What food has become cheaper? Which households have received support? What projects have been completed? How much has been spent, by whom and under what criteria? Announcements will not be sufficient. The electorate needs receipts. The opposition’s unity problem While the APC prepares a major campaign launch, opposition parties are again discussing a consensus candidate. Representatives of the ADC, NDC, PRP, SDP, APM and PDP have inaugurated legal and media committees to develop a framework for cooperation. Atiku, Peter Obi, Donald Duke and Adewale Adebayo are among the names mentioned in the talks. Coalition organisers say negotiations are progressing towards a single candidate. That claim should be treated cautiously. The Independent National Electoral Commission has already published 18 presidential candidates, including Atiku for the ADC and Obi for the NDC. Agreeing that the opposition should unite is therefore much easier than determining who withdraws, who leads, what happens to the running mates and how supporters are transferred between parties. There is also no guarantee that voters will follow elite instructions. An Atiku endorsement of Obi would not automatically deliver Atiku’s northern vote. An Obi endorsement of Atiku would not automatically transfer younger urban voters or the South-East. Nigerian politicians often mistake negotiations among leaders for consolidation among electorates. The opposition nevertheless understands the arithmetic. Tinubu won in 2023 with 36.61 per cent of the valid votes; 8.79 million votes. Atiku and Obi together received more than 13 million. That does not mean a joint ticket would have automatically defeated Tinubu, because elections are shaped by turnout, geography and the constitutional requirement for national spread. But it shows why fragmentation remains the APC’s quiet ally. Unless the coalition produces a credible agreement quickly, it risks becoming a committee for managing defeat. The register question The emphasis on 103.43 million voters has also reopened an important transparency dispute. INEC says the total follows the addition of approximately 10.77 million new registrants. Atiku has demanded that the preliminary register be made available for public inspection, alleging that an online page intended for that purpose was empty. The allegation does not establish manipulation. Technical delays or publication problems are not evidence of a compromised register. But INEC should resolve the issue immediately. A national figure cannot substitute for a register that citizens and parties can scrutinise. The public must be able to identify duplicate entries, deceased persons, omissions and questionable registrations before the final roll is certified. If parties are already building campaign strategies around precise regional totals, voters deserve access to the underlying data. First, watch the language and attendance at Saturday’s Kaduna rally. A large gathering will demonstrate organisational capacity, but the more important question is whether influential northern leaders offer genuine commitments or merely perform ceremonial loyalty. Second, watch whether the 90-day economic plan produces identifiable benefits before election day. Its political credibility will depend on outcomes, not intentions. Third, watch the opposition negotiations. A consensus announced after ballots and campaign loyalties have hardened may be largely symbolic. Finally, watch INEC. Publication and scrutiny of the voter register will be an early test of whether the Commission intends to manage doubts proactively or react only after they become political crises. The APC is campaigning on structure and patience. The opposition is campaigning on hardship and change, but without yet agreeing on whose change. item.description: Hundreds of protests were held in France Saturday as nationwide anger grows over the cost of living, with security forces massing to prevent a repeat of violence that marred demonstrations last week. Here are the latest developments: – ‘Calm’ in Paris – French police had arrested 135 people nationwide and seized a variety of weapons, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, adding that, so far, “there has been no major incident”. Weapons confiscated included metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, he said. Paris police described the situation as “calm” at midday. – ‘Scandalous’ – Hundreds of demonstrators could be seen gathering at Porte d’Italie in Paris, where authorities have said they must begin the only authorised march. Union representative Murielle Guilbert told reporters it was “scandalous” that President Emmanuel Macron had forbidden protesters from demonstrating “where we wish to demonstrate”. “We are here today, quite obviously, because there is immense social anger in this country, and because wages have still not been increased to the level they should be,” she added. Paris police at the last minute ordered the union-organised march be moved from Bastille, in the centre, to the more remote Porte d’Italie on the southeastern rim. Unions said they reluctantly agreed. But the Yellow Vests — a loosely organised group that staged disruptive street protests against Macron eight years ago — indicated they would not comply. – Halloween protests called – One group organising Saturday’s demonstrations — the Yellow Vests — said they would hold another round of protests on October 31. Organisers called for rallies and a sit-in outside parliament and city halls nationwide, condemning the “authoritarian drift” of President Emmanuel Macron’s government and urging citizens to stand up for “public freedoms”. – Tear gas in Lyon – Police fired teargas to disperse some 150 people protesting in the southeastern city of Lyon, in an area banned to all demonstrations, an AFP journalist saw. Police fired several teargas grenades to clear the group near a university faculty and the city’s police station as part of nationwide rallies against the cost of living. Police moved in as demonstrators tried to block a road. – ‘Macron resign’ – Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the city of Orleans against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw. The protest criticised both leading presidential candidate Le Pen and centrist Macron. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled. – Louvre, Orsay closed – The Louvre, d’Orsay, and Picasso museums, as well as the Grand Palais in Paris, were closed Saturday. The culture ministry had called on institutions to take every measure to ensure the safety of visitors and staff, and the protection of artworks. A country that ranks highly in one category may occupy a lower position in another, highlighting the different priorities and capabilities of armed forces worldwide. Japan’s 2026 defence white paper also highlights the security challenges surrounding the Korean Peninsula and the military capabilities maintained by North Korea. Tank Ranks by Country China leads the ranking of countries with the largest tank inventories, followed by Russia, while North Korea occupies third place ahead of the United States. The figures illustrate the importance several countries continue to place on land-based military operations, although the number of tanks alone does not determine the effectiveness of an armoured force. Russia has 5,870 tanks, while China follows closely with 5,630. North Korea ranks third with 4,895 tanks, ahead of the United States, which has 4,666. India occupies fifth place with 3,913 tanks, followed by Egypt with 3,620. Pakistan ranks seventh with 2,677, while Iran is eighth with 2,675. Türkiye takes ninth place with 2,284 tanks, and Vietnam rounds out the top 10 with 1,999. North Korea’s extensive tank inventory reflects its long-standing focus on conventional ground warfare. Research published by the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) indicates that the country operates a combination of older Soviet-inspired designs and newer equipment. Maintaining a large number of tanks can provide a military with substantial ground-firepower capacity. However, the age and technological sophistication of the vehicles also matter. Modern armour, targeting systems, sensors, weapons and battlefield communications can significantly affect the performance of tanks in combat. Consequently, a country with a larger inventory does not necessarily possess a more effective armoured force than one with fewer but more advanced vehicles. Military Aircraft The United States has the world’s largest military aircraft inventory, with 13,032 aircraft, placing it far ahead of other countries. Its fleet is more than three times the size of Russia’s and exceeds the combined totals of the next four countries in the ranking. Russia comes second with 4,237 military aircraft, followed by China with 3,529. India ranks fourth with 2,183, while South Korea occupies fifth place with 1,540. Pakistan follows with 1,429 aircraft, ahead of Japan, which has 1,397. Türkiye ranks eighth with 1,101, while Egypt has 1,088. France completes the top 10 with 974 military aircraft. The ranking includes aircraft across military branches, covering helicopters, transport planes, training aircraft and other military aviation assets, rather than combat jets alone. The United States’ substantial advantage reflects the requirements of maintaining military operations across multiple regions of the world. Its armed forces need to transport troops, equipment and supplies over long distances while supporting combat missions far from home bases. These operations depend on a broad aviation network that includes cargo aircraft, aerial refuelling tankers, helicopters and fighter jets. The ability to transport personnel and equipment and keep aircraft supplied with fuel is essential to sustaining military operations overseas. However, the difference between the United States and China becomes smaller when the comparison is restricted to fighter and interceptor aircraft. The United States has 1,791 fighters and interceptors, compared with China’s 1,443. This gives Washington an advantage of approximately 24 per cent in this category. The narrower gap demonstrates that the United States’ lead in total military aircraft is partly attributable to the size and diversity of its wider aviation fleet, rather than fighter aircraft alone. Naval Assets China has the world’s largest navy by the number of vessels in the Global Firepower ranking, with 841 naval assets. The United States follows with 465, while Russia ranks third with 343. The ranking reflects China’s expanding maritime capabilities and its extensive shipbuilding industry. Research by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) has examined how China’s commercial shipbuilding infrastructure can also support military ship production, providing an industrial foundation for expanding its naval fleet. North Korea ranks fourth with 338 naval assets, followed by Sweden with 332. Indonesia occupies sixth place with 304 vessels, while Italy ranks seventh with 285. India is eighth with 279 naval assets, Thailand ranks ninth with 275, and Sri Lanka completes the top 10 with 275 vessels. China’s total of 841 vessels is substantially higher than the United States’ 465, but vessel counts provide only one measure of naval strength. The figures include different types of vessels, ranging from small patrol boats and coastal craft to larger warships. Each vessel contributes one unit to the total, regardless of its size, armament or operational role. As a result, a country with numerous smaller vessels may rank above another whose fleet contains fewer but significantly larger and more capable ships. The ranking changes when naval strength is measured by total fleet tonnage instead of vessel numbers. Under Global Firepower’s fleet-tonnage ranking, the United States takes first place, with approximately 2.6 times China’s total displacement. Fleet tonnage measures the combined displacement of a navy’s vessels and provides a different perspective on the scale of its maritime assets. Nevertheless, tonnage also has limitations. It does not independently measure a vessel’s weapons, technological sophistication, operational readiness or combat effectiveness. item.title: FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election
item.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of member associations in his bid for re-election despite criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) rallied behind Infantino on Friday in a significant boost to the 56-year-old’s hopes of winning a fourth term in charge. Infantino’s future in the role was in doubt two months ago when he faced a furious backlash to his plan to sell off a portion of the commercial rights of competitions run by football’s world governing body to private investors. The heads of European football’s governing body UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, which runs the game in North and Central America, signed a letter saying football “belongs to no individual”. But Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, is now in a strong position to secure re-election in March. “I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view,” Infantino told the BBC on Saturday. “But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority. “I’m just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I’m speaking to all associations everywhere in the world.” No other candidate has yet come forward to oppose Infantino with the deadline to do so less than a month away on November 18. He added: “There are different points of view it’s not always easy to bring them all under one roof but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views and then it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run.” The post FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election appeared first on Vanguard News .

We’re in small groups — sometimes just pairs — trying to share updates and find other people, but it’s extremely difficult.” People gather with city hall employees and elected officials outside Lille’s town hall as part of a day of rallies called by the French Mayors’ Association (AMF) to condemn the “very serious and premeditated acts” following October’s 17 violence at town halls and calling for “a change to the police’s operational doctrine”, in Lille, north of France, on October 17, 2026. ‘Still Open’ Near Paris’s Bastille square, a clothing store removed all its merchandise ahead of the demonstrations, while a nearby restaurant was boarded up despite signs insisting it was “still open”. Many retailers in the capital had wooden boards covering windows. A heavy police presence could be seen in Place de la Bastille, along with many journalists, but few protesters. Police used a megaphone to tell the crowd that the demonstration had been banned from the area, telling protesters to go to the alternate route near Porte d’Italie “immediately”. Saint-Denis Mayor Bally Bagayoko (bottom C) attends a demonstration “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the Congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France on October 24, 2026. – Not ‘Just One Grievance’ “I don’t think the French people have just one grievance,” said Aliyah, 22, sitting with her mother Ludovine on a cafe terrace near the Old Port in Marseille as they waited for demonstrations. She said people’s primary concern was rising costs. “The people are growing poorer, the people are unhappy, so they take to the streets to protest,” she said, adding that bans on the demonstrations in some cities “only makes us more determined to show up”. ‘Curiosity’ Protests were prohibited in the city of Grenoble, with shops and restaurants open mid-morning — though a curfew was in place in parts of the city and several shopping centres from 6:00 pm (1600 GMT). Francois-Xavier Chambron, who works at a bar on the city’s Place Grenette, said they planned to stay open at least for lunch, noting that they already had reservations and that people will be around “out of sheer curiosity”. Protesters stand at the Campo Santo Antifascist village as part of a demonstration “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the Congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) with the Orleans Cathedral in the background in Orleans, central France on October 24, 2026. ‘Hotter Than Fascists’ Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the city of Orleans against a congress by the far-right National Rally (RN) party of Marine Le Pen. The protest criticised both leading presidential candidate Le Pen and centrist President Emmanuel Macron. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled, while carrying placards that read “The Youth say ‘screw you’ to the National Rally” and “Hotter than fascists”. Tear Gas In Lyon Police fired tear gas to disperse about 150 protesters in the southeastern city of Lyon, in an area banned to all demonstrations, an AFP journalist saw. Police fired several tear gas grenades to clear the group gathered at a university building and the city police station. Police moved in as protesters tried to block a road. Earlier, a police helicopter could be seen flying over the city, with security forces patrolling and armoured vehicles and riot police vans parked nearby. Shops were boarded up, with private security guards in front of some. Calls to defy the bans on protests in the city centre had circulated on social media. ‘Improvise’ Shopkeepers in boarded-up Paris said they were unsure what to expect. “It feels like we’re all just going to have to improvise a bit… We’ve secured everything as best we can, we’ll likely close at 1:00 pm and then stay in the vicinity to keep an eye on things,” Armelle Gueganton, a bookseller in the 12th arrondissement, told AFP. She worried about the route that authorities had mandated for the main Paris rally, pointing out that parts of it were “extremely narrow” and that it passed by a petrol station. “I have to wonder if they even have Google Maps at the prefecture when they authorise routes like this.” ‘Break Things’ Shops were also boarded up in the southwestern city of Bordeaux. “Boarding up five storefronts like ours … costs us nearly 5,000 euros ($5,600),” Margaux Rey, manager of the Altermundi shop, told AFPTV. “There is a high demand for securing shops ahead of the upcoming demonstrations,” confirmed Joseph Fernandez, a tradesman who was “scrambling” to meet the requests — though, he added, if individuals “want to break things, they will”. A protester speaks in a microphone as others hold a banner reading “neither congress nor meeting for the RN” during a demonstration “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the Congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France on October 24, 2026. On Patrol Numerous riot police vans could be seen in Marseille, along with armoured vehicles and water cannon. Philippe Mamelli, 64, said he was “patrolling” the southern port city’s thoroughfares armed with a truncheon at his waist and pepper spray in his pocket before heading to a demonstration later. He said he was part of a group called “Citizen Revolution” which sought to support the student protesters, adding: “The rioters are undermining” the student demands. Protesters take part in a demonstration “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the Congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France on October 24, 2026. –

item.title: 2027: Jigawa APC unveils campaign structure, names Namadi chairman
item.description: ‎ By Muhammad Inuwa ,Dutse ‎ The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Jigawa State has unveiled its campaign structure for the 2027 general elections, appointing Governor Umar Namadi as chairman and former governors Ali Sa’adu Birnin Kudu and Ibrahim Saminu Turaki as deputy chairmen. ‎ The structure is designed to coordinate campaign activities, strengthen party structures and mobilise grassroots support across the state’s 27 local government areas ahead of the elections. ‎ The appointments were announced in a statement dated October 22, 2026, and signed by the state APC chairman, Hon. Ahmed Garba. ‎ According to the statement, the party’s State Working Committee approved the composition of the campaign council following consultations with party leaders and stakeholders across the state. ‎ The council has six vice chairmen representing the three senatorial districts, with two representatives from each zone to ensure broad participation and effective coordination of campaign activities. ‎ For Jigawa North-East, Senator Muhammad Ibrahim and Senator Ibrahim Hassan Hadejia were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II, respectively. ‎ In Jigawa South-West, the Speaker of the Jigawa State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, and Hon. Farouk Adamu Aliyu were named Vice Chairmen I and II. ‎ Similarly, Alhaji Jisa Gerawa and Hajiya Rabi Ishaq were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II for Jigawa North-West Senatorial District. ‎ The party also named Alhaji Lawan Yau Roni as director-general of the campaign council, responsible for coordinating its day-to-day activities and implementing campaign programmes. ‎ The council is expected to provide strategic direction, coordinate campaign operations and strengthen engagement with party leaders, members and supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ Garba urged members of the council, party leaders and supporters to demonstrate unity, discipline, loyalty and commitment to the party’s electoral objectives. ‎ He reaffirmed the APC’s commitment to progressive governance, democratic development and advancing the interests of the people of Jigawa State, while calling on members to work together towards the party’s success in the forthcoming elections.
